Hi Marlene, it is Giulia from Hotel Firenze. You asked me about markets in Florence. There are two you should visit. The first is the Mercato Centrale. Downstairs there are food stalls with fresh fruit, cheese and olive oil. You can buy half a kilo of cheese or a bottle of oil to take home. Upstairs there are small restaurants. The second is the San Lorenzo market, on the streets outside. It has leather bags, jackets and scarves. Some things are handmade in Florence, but some are not, so ask the seller. It is OK to ask for a better price there, but always be polite. The markets open at nine. Have fun.

Welcome to the Mercato Centrale, everybody. Please stay together, because it is very busy this morning. On your left, you can see the cheese stalls. Pecorino is a cheese from Tuscany, and it is very popular. You can buy a piece of pecorino for about eight euros. On your right there are fresh vegetables and fruit. Tomatoes are cheap in September, about two euros a kilo. At the end of the hall there is a stall with olive oil. A small bottle is a nice souvenir, and it is easy to carry in your suitcase. We meet again at this door at eleven o'clock. Enjoy the market.

First, you walk to the Mercato Centrale in the morning. Then you buy half a kilo of fresh tomatoes and a piece of cheese. Next, you go to the San Lorenzo market and you look at the leather bags. After that, you ask the seller if the bag is handmade. Finally, you buy a scarf as a souvenir, and it is a real bargain.
